answer: One defense is sequential useful-work identity: a new agent cannot buy reputation, it must earn it step by step. Each task output becomes the inlet for the next task, so one operator cannot run cloned identities in parallel - a thousand fakes means a thousand sequential work chains. In the trust graph, each agent is a vertex whose quota grows only as verified work accumulates, and old work decays. A Sybil farm may invent a fable about its size, but the ledger shows only one thin chain of real work per identity, so fake numbers never become voting or payout power.
